entries.subject: DAMIT 146: selected shape and spin
entries.finding: The official DAMIT metadata export was joined by model and asteroid identity and compared with the selected local recipe shape/model-146.txt. Model 146, version 2011-04-19, pole (164°, -28°), period 13.00079 h match the retained metadata. The archive supplies no diameter for this model; a separate scale constraint is required. This comparison checks source identity and metadata, not fresh mesh bytes, registration or the completeness of other archives.

entries.subject: DAMIT documentation
entries.finding: [DAMIT documentation](https://damit.cuni.cz/pages/documentation) — coordinate units, pole, period and diameter semantics. CC BY 4.0.

entries.subject: J. Ďurech et al. (2009), Asteroid models from combined sparse and dense photometric data
entries.finding: [J. Ďurech et al. (2009), Asteroid models from combined sparse and dense photometric data](https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2009A%26A...493..291A) — original model publication record.

entries.subject: Hanuš (2011), A study of asteroid pole-latitude distribution based on an extended set of shape models derived by the lightcurve inversion method
entries.finding: [Hanuš (2011), A study of asteroid pole-latitude distribution based on an extended set of shape models derived by the lightcurve inversion method](https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2011A%26A...530A.134H) — original model publication record.

entries.subject: AKARI AcuA
entries.finding: [AKARI AcuA](https://data.darts.isas.jaxa.jp/pub/akari/AKARI-IRC_Catalogue_AllSky_AcuA_1.0/) — excluded from physical scaling because the shape-aware VS-TPM fit is available. Its fitted nonrotating-sphere diameter is 64.01 ± 0.73 km. Formal catalog error omits additional shape, spin and thermal-model effects; no total confidence interval is invented. The original catalogue row for asteroid 82 was retrieved again and matched field-for-field with the retained row, including diameter, reported error and detection count.
entries.revisitWhen: New evidence invalidates the selected shape-aware thermal fit or establishes that an effective-sphere diameter is the appropriate physical scale.

entries.subject: Resolved-model surveys: body-specific candidate not established
entries.finding: The imported survey cites Hanuš 2017, Viikinkoski 2017 and Vernazza 2021 without identifying a selected product for this body. The current DAMIT reference join does not bind selected model 146 to those surveys. This does not prove that no resolved model exists elsewhere; a body-specific candidate and its release must be identified before the entry can count as included.
entries.revisitWhen: A target row, supplementary model or release URL from one of these surveys establishes a concrete candidate and permits comparison with the selected shape.

entries.subject: Hanuš et al. 2018
entries.finding: [Hanuš et al. 2018](https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.06116) and [occultation dimensions](https://www.asteroidoccultation.com/observations/Asteroid_Dimensions_from_Occultations.html) — VS-TPM selected for this pole family; occultation ellipsoids are not silently substituted for mesh volume.

entries.subject: Registered surface imagery
entries.finding: The release supplies no registered surface imagery; the grid marks that gap.
entries.revisitWhen: A released, reusable surface observation or mapped product with registration to this body’s selected source model; the existing grid alone does not imply that every archive was searched.

entries.subject: Shape and spin alternatives
entries.finding: Only a uniform scale from the published thermophysical fit is transferred to the archived nominal mesh. The varied-model ensemble does not establish identical mesh bytes or local surface accuracy. The alternative pole remains possible. No thermal or reflectance map is inferred. Alternative archive solutions: model 147, pole ['349', '-33'], [Model 147](https://damit.cuni.cz/projects/damit/asteroid_models/view/147) The live DAMIT export lists these other models for this target: 147: pole (349°, -33°), 13.00079 h, version 2011-04-19. These are archive alternatives, not necessarily newly released models or preferred replacements. Comparing their source methods and any pole-specific calibration remains necessary before changing the selected mesh.
entries.revisitWhen: A released numerical replacement or independent pole/size constraints that distinguish the recorded alternatives, followed by comparison against the currently selected model.
